scope: Course-owned draft for teacher review of open responses. No automatic proof grading, academic approval, authenticated teacher route, persisted grade or production readiness is claimed. L04-L06 comparison tasks also require teacher-reviewed reasoning alongside relation correctness.

scoringInstructions.criterionScoring: Award each of four independent one-point criteria only when evidenced in student work; otherwise award zero for that criterion.
scoringInstructions.equivalence: Accept mathematically equivalent reasoning and representations; do not require exact phrasing.
scoringInstructions.invalidResponses: No credit for contradictory reasoning, impossible domains, or unsupported numeric guesses on criteria requiring justification.
scoringInstructions.humanDecision: Final points and explanation require an authenticated teacher/reviewer after a real student submission; this file itself does not implement that workflow.

criteria.requirement: Verify both 3 and 5 are positive and b=2>1.
State log_2(3)<log_2(5).
Explain log base 2 is increasing because 2^t is strictly increasing.
Give a valid power bound or inverse exponential comparison, not just a decimal.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: A correct increasing exponential inverse/ordering argument; optional 1<log_2(3)<log_2(5)<3 bound.
rubrics.invalidExamples: A '>' relation; comparing without validating base/arguments; a numeric-only answer.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Score the direction AND mathematical justification from actual student work; do not award reasoning credit from a single relation symbol or a numeric approximation.

criteria.requirement: Verify positive inputs 3, 5 and valid base 0.5 strictly between 0 and 1.
Explain the logarithm is decreasing and reverses order for increasing positive arguments.
Explain both results are negative because inputs exceed 1 and base 0.5<1.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: Proof by the decreasing exponential inverse and sign reasoning, without calculator dependency.
rubrics.invalidExamples: A '<' relation; treating base below one as increasing; numeric-only assertion.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Score the direction AND mathematical justification from actual student work; do not award reasoning credit from a single relation symbol or a numeric approximation.

criteria.requirement: Confirm arguments 3>1 and valid distinct bases 4 and 2.
Establish log_4(3)=log_2(3)/2 via change of base or 4=2^2.
Conclude 0<log_4(3)<log_2(3) using log_2(3)>0.
State this strict comparison is not universal for all x>0: x=1 gives equality and 0<x<1 reverses the inequality.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: Any exact equivalent change-of-base argument with correct x=1 and 0<x<1 boundary interpretation.
rubrics.invalidExamples: A reversed '>' relation at x=3; universal all-positive comparison; approximate decimals without rationale.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Score the direction AND mathematical justification from actual student work; do not award reasoning credit from a single relation symbol or a numeric approximation.

criteria.requirement: State x>0, y>0, b>0 and b!=1 for real logarithms.
Let u=log_b(x), v=log_b(y), so b^u=x and b^v=y.
Use b^(u+v)=b^u b^v=xy, a valid positive argument.
Apply uniqueness/inverse to infer log_b(xy)=u+v, not log_b(x+y); justify the equality.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: Equivalent derivation using the exponent law or valid change of base with its domain restrictions.
rubrics.invalidExamples: A decimal example or unreasoned rule statement, a false log-of-sum identity, or invalid real-log domains.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Reviewer records scored criteria, mathematical explanation and student-visible feedback. Numeric or keyword matching alone cannot certify reasoning.

criteria.requirement: Identify infinitely many solutions, not unique or inconsistent.
Provide x=2-t, y=t for all real t, or an equivalent free-variable description.
Verify both equations using the proposed family; the second is twice the first.
Explain why determinant zero does not imply no solution and why an inverse cannot be used.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: Any correct one-parameter solution family plus a mathematically justified dependence argument.
rubrics.invalidExamples: Unique solution, no solutions, a single unqualified ordered pair, or an invented inverse matrix.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Reviewer records scored criteria, mathematical explanation and student-visible feedback. Numeric or keyword matching alone cannot certify reasoning.

criteria.requirement: Identify R2 <- R2 - 2R1 as replacement of one equation by itself minus twice another.
Show that every solution of the original pair also satisfies the replaced equation.
Show reversibility by R2 <- R2 + 2R1 while retaining R1, so no solutions are lost.
Conclude the two systems have exactly the same solution set; do not assert a change in rank or solution set.

rubrics.acceptedReasoning: Equivalent algebraic substitution or a correctly described sequence of reversible elementary row operations.
rubrics.invalidExamples: A matrix or numeric answer only; stating that row operations work without explaining why; multiplying an equation by zero.
rubrics.feedbackPolicy: Reviewer records scored criteria, mathematical explanation and student-visible feedback. Numeric or keyword matching alone cannot certify reasoning.
